text.name: Text

text.emptyHint: Describe what you need: a script, title ideas, a video description. Pick the format below.
text.examples:
Five title ideas for a home coffee brewing guide
A 60-second script about saving money on groceries

image.name: Image
image.description: Thumbnails and visuals from a prompt
image.emptyHint: Describe what should be in the picture, the light and the mood. Choose the shape and how many below.
image.examples:

Studio portrait of a presenter, soft side light
A minimal desk setup from above, morning light

video.name: Video
video.description: A short clip from a prompt
video.emptyHint: Describe one shot: what moves, where the camera goes. Pick the shape and length below.

empty.title: An empty canvas
empty.description: Put cards on it. Each card works on its own: write what you want, run it, and the result stays on the card.

missing.title: This canvas is not here
missing.description: It may have been deleted, or it was made in another browser. Canvases are kept on the device they were made on.

text.titles:
{topic}: what nobody tells you
I tried {topic} for 30 days
{topic} in 5 simple steps
Stop doing {topic} like this
The only {topic} video you need
{topic}, explained in 8 minutes
text.script:
HOOK — "You're getting {topic} wrong, and it takes ten seconds to fix."
INTRO — Say who you are and what the viewer gets by the end: {topic}, without the guesswork.
STEP 1 — Show the most common mistake, then the fix, side by side.
STEP 2 — One detail that makes the biggest difference; slow it down on screen.
STEP 3 — A quick test the viewer can do at home today.
CLOSE — Sum it up in one sentence and ask what they want to see next.
text.description:
In this video: {topic}. We go through it step by step, with the mistakes to avoid and the small changes that matter most.
Save it for later, and tell us in the comments how it went for you.
Chapters: 0:00 Intro · 0:40 The basics · 3:10 Common mistakes · 6:20 Tips
text.free:
{topic} comes down to a few clear choices. Start with what the viewer already knows, then show the one thing they are missing.
Keep each point short and visual: one idea per scene, one example per idea.
Finish with a small action the viewer can take today, so the video stays with them.

link.title: What {host} is about
link.summary: The page walks through its subject in a clear order: a strong opening, three main points, and a short call to action at the end.
link.points:
The opening question pulls the viewer in within the first 10 seconds.
Each section has a single on-screen example.
The thumbnail and the title promise the same thing.
Ends with a question that brings comments.
